version_ref.description: The version, by its document and number.

media_type.description: The media type of document_text, such as text/markdown or application/json.

conforms_to.description: The schema or profile document_text follows, such as a repository's metadata schema.

document_text.description: The content of the document, as text; a structured record is serialised.

version_ref.description: The version, by its document and number.

document_title.description: A short name a person can tell documents apart by, such as README for raw/.

media_type.description: The media type of document_text, such as text/markdown or application/json.

document_text.description: The content of the document, as text; a structured record is serialised.

version_state.description: Whether a person has approved or rejected the version, or not yet decided.

decision_reason.description: The reason the person gave for their decision, in their words. Present for a rejection, and for an approval only if they gave one.

DocumentKind.title: DocumentKind

document_id.description: The identifier the conductor minted for the document, a UUIDv7.

version.description: The number of a version within its document, counted from 1.

answered_question.description: The question_id of the question answered.

answer_text.description: The answer as the person gave it.

ExternalIdentifier.description: An identifier from another scheme, as an ORCID record gives it: for a researcher, such as a Scopus Author ID; for a work, such as a DOI.

identifier_type.description: The scheme, in ORCID's words, such as doi or Scopus Author ID.

identifier_url.description: The identifier as a URL, where the record gives one.

ExternalIdentifier.title: ExternalIdentifier

FileInventory.description: The facts about a dataset's files that the project holds in place of the files (docs/specs/projects.md): for each file its path, size, digest and format, and for a table its fields. Made by a command run where the data live; it never contains a file's content. advisor.files reads it.

schema_class.description: Type designator: the name of the class this object is an instance of. Discriminates the input and payload unions, and lets a consumer name a payload class it does not recognise.

inventory_files.description: Every file under the dataset's root folder that the command read, sorted by path.

inventory_tool.description: The command that made the inventory, such as dd-inventory.

inventory_tool_version.description: The version of the command that made the inventory.

inventory_identified_with.description: What identified the formats, such as fido 1.6.1 with PRONOM signatures v109, or that only file extensions were used.

inventory_limitations.description: What the inventory left out or could not do, such as files it skipped.

FileInventory.title: FileInventory

FileRole.description: What part a file plays in a dataset, as the researcher states it (docs/specs/projects.md).
FileRole.title: FileRole

IdentificationMethod.description: How a file's format was identified, from strongest to weakest (docs/specs/projects.md).
IdentificationMethod.title: IdentificationMethod

InventoryFile.description: One file of a dataset, as the inventory command found it.

file_path.description: The file's path relative to the dataset's root folder, with forward slashes. Never an absolute path, which would say where the data live.

file_sha256.description: The SHA-256 digest of the file's bytes, in lowercase hex, by which the file deposited can be shown to be the file described.

file_media_type.description: The file's media type (MIME type), when it could be told.

file_pronom_ids.description: Every PRONOM unique identifier (PUID) the file matched, such as fmt/95 or x-fmt/18. More than one means the identification is ambiguous; none means the format is unknown.

file_identified_by.description: How the PRONOM identifiers were arrived at: by the inventory command, or chosen by the researcher where the command found several matches or none.

file_fields.description: For a table, its fields as a Frictionless Table Schema inferred from a sample of rows.

file_description.description: What the file is, in the researcher's words. The inventory command never fills it; a researcher states it beside the facts the command found (docs/specs/projects.md).

file_role.description: What part the file plays in the dataset, as the researcher states it. Unset means not stated, not data.

InventoryFile.title: InventoryFile

Obligation.description: Whether a requirement set's field or document stops a package (docs/specs/deposit.md).
Obligation.title: Obligation

RepositoryRequirements.description: The requirements of the repository a researcher chose: its standard's set with the repository's override, if there is one, merged on top (ADR-0038 decision 2). The harness makes it when the choice is recorded, keeps it among the project's blobs, gives it to the drafters and checks the project against it. Not a set of the deployment's configuration, so it has no requirement_set_id of its own; requirement_sets names the sets it was merged from.

re3data_id.description: The repository's re3data identifier, such as r3d100012124.

repository_name.description: What the researcher calls the repository chosen, such as ORDA.

conforms_to.description: The URI of the metadata schema of the standard's set.

requirement_sets.description: The sets the requirements were merged from, the standard's first.

fields.description: The metadata properties the set requires or recommends.

required_documents.description: The document kinds that must have an approved version before a package is built.

recommended_documents.description: The document kinds whose absence is a warning.

media_types.description: An override only: the media types the repository accepts. Empty means any.

max_file_size.description: An override only: the largest file the repository accepts, in bytes.

max_item_size.description: An override only: the largest deposit the repository accepts, in bytes.

licences.description: An override only: the licences the repository offers, each an SPDX identifier or the URL of the repository's own terms.

warnings.description: What the researcher was told when the repository was chosen, such as that it does not list DataCite.

unconfirmed.description: What the set's sources leave open, each a short statement naming the issue that will settle it, such as "Whether ORDA's form makes any other field mandatory (#385)". Shown to the person depositing; in a merged set, the standard's first, then the override's.

repository_url.description: Where the chosen repository is, taken from its override's url; absent when the deployment has no override for it.

RepositoryRequirements.title: RepositoryRequirements

RequirementField.description: One metadata property a requirement set requires or recommends.

property.description: The schema's property, such as DataCite's titles or types.resourceTypeGeneral.

qualifier.description: Values that narrow the property, such as a subjectScheme. Part of what identifies a field when an override is merged with its standard's set.

schema_org.description: The schema.org term the property maps to, by which the record is read as RDF.

form_label.description: An override only: the label of the repository's deposit form field the value goes in.

RequirementField.title: RequirementField

RequirementSetUse.description: One requirement set a choice of repository was merged from, as the deployment held it.

sha256.description: The SHA-256 digest of the set's file, in lowercase hex.

RequirementSetUse.title: RequirementSetUse

ResearcherFunding.description: One grant or award on an ORCID record, with its funder.

put_code.description: ORCID's identifier for the item within the record, by which a researcher chose to keep it.

funding_type.description: The kind of funding, in ORCID's words, such as grant or award.

funder_identifier.description: The funder's identifier, where ORCID gives one, such as a Crossref Funder ID.

funder_identifier_scheme.description: The scheme of funder_identifier, in ORCID's words, such as FUNDREF or ROR. Present exactly when funder_identifier is.

award_identifier.description: The grant number or award identifier, where the record gives one.

end_year.description: The year it ended; absent while it continues.

ResearcherFunding.title: ResearcherFunding

ResearcherLink.description: A web page the researcher lists on their ORCID record, such as a personal page.

link_title.description: The name the researcher gave the page.

ResearcherLink.title: ResearcherLink

ResearcherRecord.description: What one researcher in a project chose to keep from their public ORCID record: only the sections and items they ticked, in ORCID's own words, never edited by a person or a model. The conductor fills the project's records into a Message and a DraftRequest so that an agent can draft creators, affiliations, subjects and funding from them (docs/specs/projects.md). Email addresses are never kept, even public ones.

orcid_id.description: The researcher's ORCID iD, as its URL, such as https://orcid.org/0000-0002-1825-0097.

researcher_name.description: The researcher's name as their ORCID record gives it: the credit name, else the given and family names. Absent when they keep their name private or did not keep it.

other_names.description: Other names the researcher is known by, as their ORCID record lists them.

biography.description: The researcher's biography, as their ORCID record gives it.

keywords.description: The researcher's own keywords for their research, as their ORCID record lists them.

country.description: A country the researcher's ORCID record names, as an ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code.

researcher_links.description: The web pages the researcher's ORCID record lists.

external_identifiers.description: The researcher's identifiers in other schemes, as their ORCID record lists them.

affiliations.description: The researcher's affiliations they kept, the current ones first.

works.description: The researcher's works they kept, the most recent first: at most 50 are offered, so that an agent's input stays bounded.

works_omitted.description: How many works the record held beyond the 50 offered. Absent when none were left out.

fundings.description: The researcher's grants and awards they kept, the current ones first.

record_retrieved_at.description: When the record was read from ORCID's public API.

record_source.description: The public API address the record was read from.

ResearcherRecord.title: ResearcherRecord

ResearcherWork.description: One work on an ORCID record, such as a journal article or a dataset.

put_code.description: ORCID's identifier for the item within the record, by which a researcher chose to keep it.

work_type.description: The work's type, in ORCID's words, such as journal-article or data-set.

publication_year.description: The year the work was published.

journal_title.description: Where the work was published, such as a journal's name.

work_identifiers.description: The work's identifiers, such as its DOI.

ResearcherWork.title: ResearcherWork

TableField.description: One field of a tabular resource, mirroring a Frictionless Table Schema field descriptor. Frictionless publishes no RDF namespace, so these slots carry see_also rather than a slot_uri (TODO(#20): revisit if Frictionless publishes term IRIs).

field_type.description: Frictionless field type (string, number, integer, boolean, date, datetime, time, duration, geopoint, ...).

TableField.title: TableField

VersionState.description: The state of one version of a project document (ADR-0035 decision 6). Every version begins proposed; once approved or rejected, it does not change.
VersionState.title: VersionState

description: What a drafter is asked for: a project document of one kind, drafted from the project's facts (docs/specs/projects.md). Every agent that returns a Document accepts it, so an agent that drafts a document can replace another without its caller changing. The project's facts are the inventory, the requirements of the repository chosen, the metadata record a person approved last and, to regenerate a document, its current version with any decision on it. In a project, the conductor puts the inventory, the requirements and the metadata record in from the project, replacing whatever the caller sent, so a caller leaves them out; outside a project, the caller sends them. In a project the conductor also fills current_version, the latest version of the project's document of that kind, or of the document redraft_document names, so a redraft is that document's next version. The answers a person recorded to the current version's questions are filled in by the conductor in the same way (docs/specs/drafting.md), and so are the researcher facts people in the project chose to keep from their public ORCID records (docs/specs/projects.md).

schema_class.description: Type designator: the name of the class this object is an instance of. Discriminates the input and payload unions, and lets a consumer name a payload class it does not recognise.

document_kind.description: The kind of document to draft.

inventory.description: The project's inventory, the latest added. In a project the conductor fills it; a caller leaves it out.

requirements.description: The requirements of the repository chosen last. In a project the conductor fills it; a caller leaves it out.

metadata_record.description: The project's metadata record, the version a person approved last, if any has been. In a project the conductor fills it; a caller leaves it out.

current_version.description: The document's latest version, when the drafter is to regenerate it. Absent for a new document.

draft_answers.description: The answers a person recorded to the current version's questions. In a project the conductor fills them; a caller leaves them out.

redraft_document.description: The project document to redraft, by its document_id, where the project holds more than one of the kind asked for. Without it the conductor gives the latest. In a project the conductor refuses a document that is not the project's or is of another kind; outside a project it is removed.

researchers.description: The researcher facts the project holds, one record for each person who kept some. In a project the conductor fills them and a caller leaves them out; outside a project, the caller sends them, as it does the other facts.

title: DraftRequest
